hed: Weekend Hormuz projectile strike feeds Monday oil jump; traffic still thin
dek: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a vessel struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz late Saturday (~2300 GMT), with a Sunday update citing fire and crew evacuation. Iranian media separately said a commercial vessel near Qeshm was hit with one dead. Monday market desks tied the weekend incident — plus Saudi Petroline’s continued outage — to Brent’s jump toward $108. Ship-tracking cited by NBC News put Sunday Hormuz transits at about 14 vessels, still a fraction of pre-war daily volumes; Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said recent average oil flows are roughly two-thirds of prior levels.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: CNBC, Anadolu Agency, and Al Jazeera pair UKMTO’s Saturday projectile alert and Sunday fire/evacuation update with Monday’s crude spike and sparse transit counts — stressing that U.S. claims of improving Hormuz escort traffic have not restored pre-war commercial volumes or ended weekend strikes.

cr.body: NBC News’s MarineTraffic counts, Al Jazeera’s Wright quote on roughly two-thirds of prior oil flows, and Anadolu’s UKMTO fire update frame Monday risk as a contested chokepoint: escorts and official flow claims versus single-digit-to-teens daily vessel counts and another weekend projectile hit.

stack_blurb: UKMTO weekend Hormuz strike + thin traffic; Monday crude surge.
seo_description: Weekend UKMTO Hormuz projectile strike and thin vessel traffic feed Monday’s oil jump as Brent nears $108; Iran separately reported a Qeshm commercial vessel hit.
